sentences.text: Heard Mr. Gite, learned counsel for the petition Mr.Samant, learned APP for the respondents - State in these petitions.
2. The petitioners are claiming that the respondents have willfully disobeyed judgement and order dated 01.03.2019 passed by a Division Bench of this Court.

As per the directions issued in the said judgement, the respondents were directed to complete acquisition proceedings in respect of determination of amount of compensation and to declare award under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: SANDIP PARAB

Since the respondents failed to take appropriate steps in the light of the specific direction issued by the Division Bench of this Court in the said judgement and order dated 01.03.2019, 17 contempt petitions were filed before this Court.

5. By an order dated 03.01.2025, 15 contempt petitions were disposed of on the basis of an affidavit filed on behalf of the Sub- Divisional Officer, Baramati to the effect that the lands of the petitioners therein were not required.

After noting the contents of the said affidavit, a Division Bench of this Court found that since the respondents themselves were no longer interested in acquisition, as a result of which, there could not be any compulsion upon the respondents to proceed with the acquisition, further steps in the contempt proceedings would not be taken against the respondents.
Accordingly, the said contempt petitions were disposed of.
6. But, in the present case, the respondents have not taken such a stand.

In fact, in the affidavit dated 18.11.2025 filed by the Sub- Divisional Officer, Baramati, it is stated that the land of the petitioners in these two petitions was already distributed to project affected persons.
It is further stated that review petitions have been filed in the context of the petitioners herein and that, there is merit in the review petitions.
7. It is an admitted position that the review petitions were filed recently in May, 2025 and they suffer from a huge delay of 6 years, 1 month and 7 days.
Applications for condonation of delay have been filed along with the review petitions and they are pending for consideration before the appropriate Bench.
8. We are of the opinion that mere filing of review petitions along with applications for condonation of delay, cannot be a ground for continued adjournment of the present proceedings.

There is nothing on record to show as to what steps the respondents have taken for having the review petitions along with applications for condonation of delay circulated and heard before the appropriate Bench.
Filing of such belated review petitions appears to be a tactic to avoid the consequences of disobedience of the judgement and order of this Court.

sentences.text: Since the Sub-Divisional Officer, Baramati is the competent authority to initiate the acquisition proceedings for abiding by the specific direction issued in the order dated 01.03.2019 passed by the Division Bench of this Court, appropriate notice to show cause as to why action ought not to be taken against the respondents for having committed contempt of this Court, needs to be issued.
11. A perusal of the contempt petitions shows that officers, only by their designation have been made parties.
At this stage, the learned counsel for the petitioners seeks leave to amend the petitions to add names of the officers, who have allegedly committed contempt of this Court.
Leave is granted to carry out the amendment forthwith.

12. In the light of the fact that respondent No.1 i.e. Sub-Divisional Officer, Baramati has filed the affidavit in the present petition referred to hereinabove, for the present, the aforesaid show cause notice be issued only to the respondent / alleged contemnor No.1.
13.

Hence, issue notice to the respondent / alleged contemnor No.1, returnable on 14.01.2026 to show cause as to why action ought not to be taken against the said respondent under the provisions of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.

(MANJUSHA DESHPANDE, J.) (MANISH PITALE, J.)
